sections.text: Protections
Technical Procedure

Equipment
 Distance Relay
 REL 316*4
 ABB
Introduction

The
 REL316*4 digital line protection scheme is designed for the
 high-speed discriminative protection of lines and cables in
 distribution and transmission systems. The rated voltage of
 the line being protected is not a restriction and the
 protection is applicable to solidly or low-resistance
 grounded systems, systems with Petersen coils or to
 ungrounded systems.

All
 kinds of faults are detected including close-in three-phase,
 cross-country faults, evolving faults and high-resistance
 earth faults

This
 procedure details the steps required to completely check the
 proper operation and calibration of the relay. It is
 recommended this procedure be carried out on an annually
 bases. The document is formatted the way to minimize the
 possibility of error causing personal injury or damage to
 equipment.

The
 first draft initiated by eng. Samah Mokhtar Mostafa,
 tested at 31 Dec 2002 by eng.Yousef Melad Shahat at Wadi Hoof station, accepted by General director eng. 
 Abdel Menem Rabie Motalaqeh,
 and approved by eng. Fawzy Mourse Mohamed:
 Head Sector of Aswan Network.
Safety Precautions

A work permit
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should
 carry the suitable safety category,

Safety fence (rope)
 with caution marks surrounding the work area,

Line isolation
 is required.

Make sure that CT
 secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the
 current circuits for test distance protection

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

Steps
to prepare for relay testing

Review
 technical reference material and manufacturer's manual

Obtain
 copy of relay setting from field maintenance file and
 compare it with the setting on the relay

Obtain
 outage for line protected by this relay

Check
 that the circuit breaker is opened and tagged

Inspect
 the CT secondary circuits, the VT miniature circuit
 breakers ( MCB's) and all cabling supplying the relaying

Use
 the station drawings to isolate the following:
 * Breaker trip coils
 * Breaker failure scheme associated with the
 relay and disturbance alarms

sections.text:
Distance
protection test

Be
 sure that the DC power of the relay is correct by
 applying a D.C voltmeter across points H2 and H3 on the
 rear of the relay

Connect
 the current test leads on the current terminals of the
 relay T1,T3,T5,T6 and the voltage test leads on the
 voltage terminals of the relay T11,T12<T13,T13

Connect
 A.C power to the test set

Inject
 current, voltage and phase angle by selecting the value
 of impedance (X)

To
 test zone (1) phase R to Neutral:
 * Take the value of (X)
 greater than the maximum value of working for zone 1 and
 decrease it slowly until the relay operates and
 the LED of (protection trip - zone 1) lights

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (1) phase S to Neutral.

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (1) phase T to Neutral.

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (1) phase R to S.

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (1) phase S to T.

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (1) phase T to R.

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (1) phase R to S To T.

To
 test zone (2) phase R to Neutral:
 * Take the value
 of (X) greater than the maximum value of working for
 zone 2 and decrease it slowly until the
 relay operates and the LED of (protection trip - zone 2)
 lights

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (2) phase S to Neutral

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (2) phase T to Neutral

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (2) phase R to S

Repeat
 step 5 to test zone (2) phase S to T

Repeat

To

 the value of (X) greater than the maximum value of

Repeat

Repeat

 step 5 to zone (3) phase R to S

Repeat
 step 5 to zone (3) phase S to T

Repeat
 step 5 to zone (3) phase T to R

Return
relay and associated equipment to service

Return
 relay to service by removing the test leads from the
 relay terminals and the test set

Make
 sure CT and V T secondary circuits are in normal
 condition

Remove
 the disturbance alarm LED`s on the relay which is caused
 by the test

Request
 feeder to be returned in service

Take
 phasor readings of all A C currents and voltages and
 compare them to those for normal load condition

Check
 that these reading agree with station meters (MW, Mvar,
 Amperes and power factor)

Place
 a copy of the testresult in the field maintenance file
